symptoms: Job fails at runtime as soon as a class from a custom JAR is loaded
ClassNotFoundException for a class that exists inside the supplied JAR
Failure appears only after changing GlueVersion to 6.0, with no code change
likely_causes: Custom JAR passed in --extra-jars was compiled against Scala 2.12; AWS Glue 6.0 runs Scala 2.13.17 and Scala minor versions are not binary compatible
Transitive dependency of the custom JAR still carries a Scala 2.12 artifact suffix (_2.12)
diagnostic_steps: Read mig.jar_binary.scala_minor for every JAR under the job directory: sparkforge glue dependency-audit <dir> --glue 6.0
Check the artifact suffix of each JAR name and of its transitive dependencies (_2.12 vs _2.13)
Confirm the job's GlueVersion in the Terraform or job definition
fixes: Recompile every custom Scala/Java JAR against Scala 2.13.17 and republish it
Replace JavaConversions with CollectionConverters and MutableList with ListBuffer; parallel collections now require a separate import
Update --extra-jars to point at the 2.13 artifacts
unsafe_fixes: Forcing the 2.12 JAR ahead of the runtime classpath with --user-jars-first: the runtime itself is 2.13, so this trades one linkage error for another
Staying on Glue 5.1 without recording the decision: it is a legitimate choice, but it has to be a declared one
verification: Run the job on AWS Glue 6.0 with the recompiled JAR and confirm the class that failed now loads
rollback: Revert GlueVersion to 5.1, where Scala 2.12.18 is the runtime; the 2.12 JAR works there unchanged
